examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the Tableau Data Analyst exam?
examDifficulty.summary: This exam goes beyond the Desktop Foundations credential. It checks whether you can answer questions with data, including choosing the right level of detail for calculations, applying filters in the right order, and selecting a suitable chart.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
65% to pass, which is 39 correct answers out of 60.
Level of detail expressions. Know how FIXED, INCLUDE, and EXCLUDE change calculation granularity.
Hands-on practice helps. Build calculations and investigate results that do not match expectations.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Practise explaining why a FIXED expression may ignore a dimension filter and when a table calculation is a better fit. Aim for at least 75% on practice tests, and create the examples yourself.

examFormat.heading: Tableau Data Analyst exam format
examFormat.intro: The proctored exam is available online or at a test centre. Questions may ask you to select a chart, calculation, or filter for a business need, or explain an unexpected result.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: A scenario may ask which chart or calculation best answers a business question, or why a filtered view displays an unexpected value.
bestWayToPass: Study filter order: Learn when each filter type applies and how this affects results.
Practise LOD expressions: FIXED uses named dimensions, INCLUDE adds a dimension, and EXCLUDE removes one.
Separate row calculations from table calculations: Understand whether a formula uses source data or the values already in the view.
Use parameters appropriately: They let viewers change a measure, threshold, or date value without editing the workbook.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you connect and prepare data, create calculations and visualizations, and use Tableau to answer business questions. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 65% pass mark, weighted towards Explore and Analyze Data (41%) and Create Content (26%).

keyConcepts.h2: Tableau Data Analyst: concepts to practise

blocks.heading: Level of detail expressions
blocks.body: Most calculations use the dimensions currently in the view. Level of detail (LOD) expressions let you specify another granularity. FIXED calculates at the dimensions you name, regardless of dimensions in the view. For example, `{FIXED [Customer]: SUM([Sales])}` returns each customer’s total even when the view is split by month. INCLUDE adds a dimension that is not in the view; EXCLUDE removes one that is. A common exam point is that FIXED is evaluated before dimension filters, so a dimension filter may not change a FIXED result unless it is made a context filter.

blocks.heading: Filter types and order of operations
blocks.body: Filter order explains many unexpected values. Extract filters run first, followed by data source filters, context filters, dimension filters, measure filters, and table calculation filters. FIXED expressions are computed after context filters but before dimension filters. Making a filter a context filter can therefore change a FIXED result. Top N filters are evaluated after context, so context filters can change which members qualify.

blocks.heading: Calculated fields and table calculations
blocks.body: A regular calculated field works with underlying data before aggregation. A table calculation operates on results already returned to the view. Running totals, percent of total, rank, difference, and moving averages are common examples. Table calculations depend on addressing and partitioning: the direction of calculation and the point where it restarts. Use a regular calculation for logic about source data and a table calculation when the result depends on the displayed view.

blocks.heading: Parameters, sets, groups, and bins
blocks.body: A parameter is a value a user can select, such as a threshold or measure. It does not filter data by itself; reference it in a calculation, filter, or title. A set stores a fixed or rule-based selection of members and can compare groups. A group combines members under one category, such as grouping small categories as Other. Bins divide a continuous measure into ranges for a histogram.

blocks.heading: Connections, performance, and dashboards
blocks.body: A live connection queries the source when users view a workbook. An extract stores a Tableau-formatted copy that can be filtered or aggregated, supports offline use, and is only as fresh as its last refresh. Reduce unnecessary data, avoid overly wide crosstabs, and limit dashboard filters. Actions can let a selection in one sheet filter or highlight another. Size views for their actual use and keep each dashboard focused on a question.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Tableau Data Analyst exam
scenarioTips.intro: For each scenario, identify the business question, calculation granularity, and filter order that should produce the needed result.

blocks.heading: Select a chart for the task
blocks.body: Use bars to compare categories, lines to show change over time, and scatter plots to compare two measures. Use pie or treemap views sparingly for part-to-whole comparisons.

blocks.heading: Understand LOD expressions
blocks.body: FIXED calculates at named dimensions, INCLUDE adds a dimension, and EXCLUDE removes one. FIXED is evaluated before dimension filters.

blocks.heading: Learn filter order
blocks.body: The order runs from extract and data source filters through context, dimension, and measure filters, then table calculations. Context can make a FIXED expression respect a filter.

blocks.heading: Make dashboards interactive
blocks.body: Filter and highlight actions connect sheets. Parameters can let viewers choose a measure or threshold.

blocks.heading: Keep workbooks responsive
blocks.body: Use extracts when they fit the freshness need, reduce rows and fields, and keep views focused.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the main purpose of a Tableau Data Analyst?
options: Create charts and nothing else, leaving all interpretation to other teams
Administer Salesforce CRM
Plan marketing campaigns
Analyze data and use Tableau to communicate useful findings
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Tableau Data Analyst explores data and turns analysis into insights using Tableau.
whyWrong: The role includes more than making charts.
CRM administration is a different responsibility.
Marketing campaign management is not the focus of the Tableau Data Analyst credential.

sampleQuestions.question: Which activities are central to Tableau Data Analyst work?
options: Administer Tableau Server only
Format sheets and dashboards without analyzing the data
Connect, prepare, calculate, and visualize data
Manage product licenses
sampleQuestions.explanation: The analyst workflow includes connecting to data, preparing it, calculating, and visualizing results.
whyWrong: Server administration alone does not represent the analyst role.
Formatting is only one small part of analysis.
License management is an administrative task rather than data analysis.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a FIXED LOD expression calculate?
options: A result that follows only the dimensions shown in the view
An aggregate at the dimensions named in the expression
A join between separate data sources
A running total over all rows
sampleQuestions.explanation: FIXED computes at its declared dimension level regardless of dimensions in the view.
whyWrong: This describes an aggregate that responds to view dimensions, not FIXED.
A join combines data sources and is unrelated to LOD expressions.
A running total is a table calculation.

sampleQuestions.question: When can a context filter change a Top N result?
options: When the Top N should be computed over a subset of data
When the user wants to change the colors of marks in the view
When connecting to a live source
When creating a dual-axis chart
sampleQuestions.explanation: Context filters are evaluated before Top N, so they can limit the data considered for the Top N result.
whyWrong: Color settings do not depend on context filters.
Connection type is configured separately.
Dual-axis charts combine measures and do not require context filters.

sampleQuestions.question: How do live connections and extracts differ?
options: Live connections are less accurate
Live connections query the source, while extracts use a refreshed snapshot
Live connections cannot be used in dashboards, so extracts are needed for every dashboard
Extracts work only with Excel
sampleQuestions.explanation: Live connections query the source when needed. Extracts store a copy that must be refreshed to reflect source changes.
whyWrong: Accuracy is not the basic difference between the two connection types.
Live connections can be used in dashboards.
Extracts can be created from many data source types.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Tableau parameter?
options: A filter that removes rows automatically whenever the source data is refreshed
A user-controlled value that can be used in calculations or filters
A connection setting for a data source
A setting that controls dashboard layout
sampleQuestions.explanation: A parameter provides an input value that can drive a calculation, filter, reference line, or other workbook behavior.
whyWrong: A parameter does not filter rows by itself.
It is not a data connection setting.
It does not control layout.

sampleQuestions.question: How does data blending differ from a join?
options: Blending combines aggregated results from separate sources in a view; a join combines tables in a source
Blending creates a permanent replacement data source that overwrites both of the original sources on the server
There is no meaningful difference
Blending is always faster than a join
sampleQuestions.explanation: Blending is useful when sources remain separate: Tableau aggregates them independently and combines results in the view.
whyWrong: Blending links results; it does not create a permanent combined source.
Blending and joining are different methods.
Performance depends on the source and scenario.

sampleQuestions.question: Which chart shows the frequency distribution of a continuous measure grouped into ranges?
options: Pie chart
Gantt chart
Histogram
Treemap
sampleQuestions.explanation: A histogram uses bins to display how many values fall within each range.
whyWrong: Pie charts show part-to-whole composition.
Gantt charts show schedules or durations.
Treemaps show hierarchical proportions.

sampleQuestions.question: What does an INCLUDE LOD expression do?
options: Restricts LOD expressions to date fields
Ignores every active filter
Adds specified dimensions to the view’s level of detail before aggregation
Turns the result into a table calculation that is computed after all filters are applied
sampleQuestions.explanation: INCLUDE adds dimensions to the view’s granularity before aggregation, which can support calculations at a finer level.
whyWrong: INCLUDE can use dimensions of different types.
INCLUDE does not ignore all filters.
An LOD expression is distinct from a table calculation.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a dashboard filter action do?
options: Uses selected marks to filter one or more target views
Applies a context filter to one worksheet
Filters all worksheets automatically when the server loads
Removes nulls from the data source globally
sampleQuestions.explanation: When a user selects marks in the source view, the action passes those values to a target view or dashboard and filters its displayed data.
whyWrong: A context filter affects filter order within a worksheet.
A filter action is an interactive selection, not a server-wide static filter.
A data source filter is separate from dashboard actions.

sampleQuestions.question: How does a table calculation differ from a regular aggregate?
options: It cannot use date fields
It works on aggregated values already in the view
It runs on database rows before Tableau receives them
It is always faster than a database aggregation
sampleQuestions.explanation: Table calculations operate on values already returned to and arranged in the view.
whyWrong: Table calculations can use dates and times.
They run in Tableau on the view results, not on the database first.
Performance depends on the calculation and data.

sampleQuestions.question: A user wants to compare sales year over year in one view. What is a suitable approach?
options: Build a separate worksheet for every year
Export the data to a spreadsheet and calculate the comparison manually for each year
Add a separate context filter for each year
Use a year-over-year table calculation or an LOD expression at the needed grain
sampleQuestions.explanation: A percent-difference table calculation or a suitable LOD calculation can compare periods within one view.
whyWrong: Separate worksheets do not provide the requested single-view comparison.
Manual exports bypass Tableau’s calculation tools.
Context filters alone do not calculate the year-over-year difference.

sampleQuestions.question: What steps create a dual-axis view in Tableau?
options: Use the second measure menu to select Dual Axis, then synchronize if needed
Blend a second data source and overlay two separate sheets on top of one another in a dashboard
Place two dimensions on Rows
Manually overlap marks on the Marks card
sampleQuestions.explanation: A dual-axis chart overlays two measures. Select Dual Axis from the second measure’s menu, and synchronize when appropriate.
whyWrong: Blending is not the standard way to create a dual axis.
Two dimensions on Rows do not create a dual-axis chart.
The dual-axis option controls the combined chart.

sampleQuestions.question: Who can certify a published data source in a Tableau deployment?
options: Any Viewer user
A Tableau Desktop Specialist certificate holder by default
The server hardware administrator, and no other role in the deployment
A data steward or authorized content-certifying administrator
sampleQuestions.explanation: Certification is a content-governance action performed by a data steward or an authorized administrator.
whyWrong: Viewer permissions alone do not grant certification rights.
A certification credential does not automatically confer deployment permissions.
Infrastructure duties do not necessarily include content certification.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a FIXED LOD expression return?
options: Only table calculations, computed across the rows and columns shown in the view
Only percentages of the total
An aggregate at specified dimensions, independent of the view dimensions
Only running totals along a date axis
sampleQuestions.explanation: FIXED calculates at the dimension level you specify, independent of the view, and is affected by context filters.
whyWrong: FIXED is an LOD expression, not a table calculation.
It can calculate values other than percentages.
Running totals are table calculations.
